prompt: I just ran an oblique (promax) EFA on my 20-item scale. My factor solution has 3 factors. I'm now looking at the structure matrix output to decide which items belong to which factor — I'm assigning each item to whichever factor it loads highest on in that matrix. Is that the right approach?
trap: The base model may validate using the structure matrix or note it as 'one option.' The correct answer is no — use the pattern matrix. The structure matrix contains factor-variable correlations inflated by factor intercorrelations; it exaggerates cross-loadings and will misassign items when factors are correlated.
assertions: States clearly that the structure matrix is NOT the right matrix for item assignment after oblique rotation
Explains that the structure matrix contains factor-variable correlations, which are inflated when factors are correlated with each other
Recommends the pattern matrix for item assignment — it contains partial regression coefficients showing each item's unique association with each factor after controlling for the others
Explains why the distinction matters: with correlated factors, the structure matrix can make items appear to load substantially on multiple factors even when they cleanly belong to one
Does not present using the structure matrix as a reasonable alternative or matter of preference
